main_text.p: ephippiis solo deturbentur ca-taphractati,lapsuque graviore, quo pondere magis obruütur, si non intereant, saltem pericu-lose lædantur. Unde etiam in-ter Græcos sapientiores, qui vel pueris talia exercitia per-miserunt, eos, ut absque peri-culo artis equestris, aliorum exercitiorum rudimenta addi-scerent, dorsis arietum, ne ex alto laberentur, imponebant.

Gabriel Naudeus libr.1. Syntagm. de studio Milit.p. 157:Metus insuper est, ne lan-ceis in adversum directis ictu quo vulnerentur, aut iisdem fractis, alibi particula cassidem subintret. Quomodo maximo cum discrimine Cesennæ exhiberi solitas fuisse illas decursiones, propter crassiores hastas & præpilatas, quibus nobiles inter se concurrebant testis est Gabriel Naudeus.
2. Quia hoc genus haftilu-dii nullam hodie utilitatem adferre poterit. Majore quippe

page.notes: Printed text read from a clear scan. Doubtful points: "obruütur" (umlaut as printed), "lose" in the line "lose lædantur", and "caßidem" read as "cassidem" from the ligature. The stray slash marks near "ha-" and "ftas" are printing marks, not text, and are left out. A small dash at the very foot is not transcribed. Catchword "cum" is the word printed at the lower right.
